4. // VirtMemoryManager — Specifications (spec phase)
5. //
6. // `VirtMemoryManager` is a zero-sized, stateless singleton façade: every
7. // observable effect lands on the `Vmem` argument(s) (modeled by the inherited
8. // `VmemView` from `mm::virt::vmem`), on returned owned RAII values
9. // (`KernelPage`, `Vec<KernelFrame>`, `Vec<UserFrame>`, a new `Vmem`), or on the
10. // global physical-frame pool (deliberately outside any View). This file
11. // therefore contributes (a) a unit manager View, and (b) the manager-level
12. // vocabulary (pure architectural predicates and range/fork transitions over
13. // `VmemView`) that the manager's `#[verus_spec]` contracts are written against.
14. //
15. // See `view_design.md` for the full rationale.
16. 
17. // Inherited abstractions from the `mm::virt::vmem` module (only available under
18. // `verus_keep_ghost`, which is exactly when this file is included).
19. use crate::mm::virt::vmem::{
20.     is_page_aligned,
21.     page_base,
22.     page_size,
23.     spec_is_physical_region,
24.     spec_is_user_addr,
25.     AddrNat,
26.     PagePerms,
27.     PermView,
28.     UserPageView,
29.     VmemView,
30. };
31. 
32. verus! {
33. 
34. //==================================================================================================
35. // External (opaque) dependency types used only by the manager's contracts
36. //
37. // These types are not modeled by `mm::virt::vmem`'s spec file. They live in
38. // lower-level / sibling crates (the x86 exception error code, the kernel-frame
39. // RAII handle, the ELF file header) and are declared `external_body` so Verus
40. // treats them as opaque. The trust obligation is discharged when those modules
41. // are verified.
42. //==================================================================================================
43. 
44. /// The x86 page-fault error code (`::arch::cpu::excp::ErrorCode`).
45. #[verifier::external_type_specification]
46. #[verifier::external_body]
47. pub struct ExExcpErrorCode(::arch::cpu::excp::ErrorCode);
48. 
49. /// RAII handle for a single kernel frame (`mm::phys::KernelFrame`).
50. #[verifier::external_type_specification]
51. #[verifier::external_body]
52. pub struct ExKernelFrame(KernelFrame);
53. 
54. /// ELF32 file header (`mm::elf::Elf32Fhdr`).
55. #[verifier::external_type_specification]
56. #[verifier::external_body]
57. pub struct ExElf32Fhdr(Elf32Fhdr);
58. 
59. //==================================================================================================
60. // Projection of the opaque page-fault error code into the abstract bit triple
61. //
62. // `is_present` / `is_write` / `is_user` are pure `const fn`s decoding hardware
63. // error-code bits. Their abstract counterparts are uninterpreted projections of
64. // the opaque external `ErrorCode` (a mechanical consequence of that type being
65. // `external_body`).
66. //==================================================================================================
67. 
68. pub trait ErrorCodeBits {
69.     spec fn ec_present(&self) -> bool;
70. 
71.     spec fn ec_write(&self) -> bool;
72. 
73.     spec fn ec_user(&self) -> bool;
74. }
75. 
76. impl ErrorCodeBits for ::arch::cpu::excp::ErrorCode {
77.     uninterp spec fn ec_present(&self) -> bool;
78. 
79.     uninterp spec fn ec_write(&self) -> bool;
80. 
81.     uninterp spec fn ec_user(&self) -> bool;
82. }
83. 
84. //==================================================================================================
85. // Abstract physical-frame projection of the opaque kernel-frame RAII handle
86. //
87. // `KernelFrame` is owned by the not-yet-verified `mm::phys` module and modeled
88. // here as opaque (`ExKernelFrame`). Its byte address is an uninterpreted
89. // projection (mechanical consequence of the type being `external_body`), letting
90. // `alloc_kpages` state per-frame validity exactly as `alloc_kpage` does for
91. // `KernelPage`.
92. //==================================================================================================
93. 
94. impl AddrNat for KernelFrame {
95.     uninterp spec fn addr_nat(&self) -> nat;
96. }
97. 
98. //==================================================================================================
99. // Pure architectural predicates (no `&self`, instance-independent)
100. //==================================================================================================
101. 
102. /// A page fault qualifies as a copy-on-write write fault: a user-mode write to a
103. /// present page. Pure decode of the x86 page-fault error-code bits. Whether the
104. /// *page* is actually CoW is read from `vmem@` separately.
105. pub open spec fn spec_is_cow_write_fault(ec: ::arch::cpu::excp::ErrorCode) -> bool {
106.     ec.ec_present() && ec.ec_write() && ec.ec_user()
107. }
108. 
109. /// Membership test for the page run `base, base + PAGE_SIZE, …, base +
110. /// (n-1)*PAGE_SIZE`: `v` is in the run iff it is a page-aligned offset from
111. /// `base` strictly below `base + n*PAGE_SIZE`.
112. pub open spec fn in_page_run(base: nat, n: nat, v: nat) -> bool {
113.     &&& base <= v
114.     &&& v < base + n * page_size()
115.     &&& (v - base) as int % page_size() as int == 0
116. }
117. 
118. /// A mapping is *logically writable* (CoW-eligible at fork time): writable in
119. /// hardware OR already CoW (left read-only with the CoW bit set by an earlier
120. /// fork). Mirrors the docstring of `link_user_pages`.
121. pub open spec fn logically_writable(p: UserPageView) -> bool {
122.     p.perms.write || p.cow
123. }
124. 
125. //==================================================================================================
126. // Range / fork shapes over `VmemView`
127. //==================================================================================================
128. 
129. /// Success shape of `alloc_upages`: exactly the run `[base, base+n*PAGE_SIZE)`
130. /// was added, each page mapped with `perms` and not CoW; everything outside the
131. /// run is bit-for-bit preserved; kernel half and page directory are untouched.
132. /// The backing frame of each new page is an allocator detail and stays
133. /// existential (not pinned here).
134. pub open spec fn maps_user_run_with(
135.     old: VmemView,
136.     new: VmemView,
137.     base: nat,
138.     n: nat,
139.     perms: PagePerms,
140. ) -> bool {
141.     // The user domain grew by exactly the run: a vaddr is mapped afterwards iff
142.     // it was mapped before or it lies in the freshly-allocated run.
143.     &&& forall|v: nat| #[trigger] new.user.contains_key(v)
144.             <==> (old.user.contains_key(v) || in_page_run(base, n, v))
145.     // Pages outside the run are bit-for-bit preserved.
146.     &&& forall|v: nat| #[trigger] old.user.contains_key(v) ==> new.user.contains_key(v)
147.             && new.user[v] == old.user[v]
148.     // Each new page has the requested perms and is private (not CoW).
149.     &&& forall|v: nat| in_page_run(base, n, v) ==> #[trigger] new.user.contains_key(v)
150.             && new.user[v].perms == perms && !new.user[v].cow
151.     // Kernel half and page directory are unchanged.
152.     &&& new.kernel == old.kernel
153.     &&& new.pgdir == old.pgdir
154. }
155. 
156. /// Caller precondition for `link_user_pages`: the child has no user mappings
157. /// overlapping the parent's (relied on by the rollback heuristic).
158. pub open spec fn link_user_pages_pre(parent: VmemView, child: VmemView) -> bool {
159.     forall|v: nat| #[trigger] parent.user.contains_key(v) ==> !child.user.contains_key(v)
160. }
161. 
162. /// Success shape of `link_user_pages` on the `(parent, child)` pair. Every
163. /// present user page of the entry parent is shared into the child at the same
164. /// vaddr and frame; logically-writable pages become CoW in BOTH parent and
165. /// child; genuinely read-only pages are shared read-only (not CoW). The child
166. /// gains exactly the parent's user domain (it had none overlapping on entry —
167. /// see `link_user_pages_pre`). Parent user frames/domain are preserved (only its
168. /// CoW marks may flip); kernel halves and page directories are unchanged.
169. pub open spec fn links_child_cow(
170.     p_old: VmemView,
171.     p_new: VmemView,
172.     c_old: VmemView,
173.     c_new: VmemView,
174. ) -> bool {
175.     // Parent domain & frames preserved; perms unchanged except CoW marking.
176.     &&& p_new.user.dom() == p_old.user.dom()
177.     &&& forall|v: nat| #[trigger] p_old.user.contains_key(v) ==> {
178.             &&& p_new.user.contains_key(v)
179.             &&& p_new.user[v].frame == p_old.user[v].frame
180.             &&& (logically_writable(p_old.user[v]) ==> p_new.user[v].cow)
181.             &&& (!logically_writable(p_old.user[v]) ==> p_new.user[v] == p_old.user[v])
182.         }
183.     // Child gains exactly the parent's user pages: same frames, CoW iff writable.
184.     &&& c_new.user.dom() == c_old.user.dom().union(p_old.user.dom())
185.     &&& forall|v: nat| #[trigger] p_old.user.contains_key(v) ==> {
186.             &&& c_new.user.contains_key(v)
187.             &&& c_new.user[v].frame == p_old.user[v].frame
188.             &&& c_new.user[v].cow == logically_writable(p_old.user[v])
189.         }
190.     // Pre-existing, non-overlapping child pages are preserved.
191.     &&& forall|v: nat| #[trigger] c_old.user.contains_key(v) && !p_old.user.contains_key(v)
192.             ==> c_new.user.contains_key(v) && c_new.user[v] == c_old.user[v]
193.     // Kernel halves and page directories unchanged on both.
194.     &&& p_new.kernel == p_old.kernel
195.     &&& p_new.pgdir == p_old.pgdir
196.     &&& c_new.kernel == c_old.kernel
197.     &&& c_new.pgdir == c_old.pgdir
198. }
199. 
200. //==================================================================================================
201. // VirtMemoryManagerView — unit View of the stateless manager singleton
202. //==================================================================================================
203. 
204. /// Abstract state of the (stateless) virtual-memory manager singleton.
205. ///
206. /// `VirtMemoryManager` is zero-sized: it owns no mappings, no frames, and no
207. /// page tables. All abstract state a caller reasons about lives in the `Vmem`
208. /// argument(s) (`VmemView`) and in the returned owned values. This marker View
209. /// therefore carries no fields — it exists only so the manager satisfies the
210. /// module's View/`inv()` convention.
211. pub struct VirtMemoryManagerView;
212. 
213. impl View for VirtMemoryManager {
214.     type V = VirtMemoryManagerView;
215. 
216.     closed spec fn view(&self) -> VirtMemoryManagerView {
217.         VirtMemoryManagerView
218.     }
219. }
220. 
221. impl VirtMemoryManager {
222.     /// Internal consistency. The manager has no internal exec fields, so there is
223.     /// no implementation-consistency obligation to encode.
224.     pub open spec fn internal_inv(&self) -> bool {
225.         true
226.     }
227. 
228.     /// Top-level invariant. There is no caller-visible manager-level
229.     /// well-formedness; per-`Vmem` well-formedness is asserted on the `Vmem`
230.     /// arguments of each method.
231.     pub open spec fn inv(&self) -> bool {
232.         self.internal_inv()
233.     }
234. }
235.

# Bugs — `mm::virt::manager`

## Context-Dependent — `link_user_pages` / `rollback_linked_pages` (manager.rs:301, :465)

**What**: The documented contract and caller analysis state that on `Err`,
`link_user_pages` restores *both* `parent` and `child` to their entry state
("any copy-on-write marks installed on `parent` are cleared"). The
implementation's rollback (`rollback_linked_pages`) deliberately does **not**
clear the parent's CoW marks and is otherwise best-effort (it logs and continues
on every unmap/unmark failure).

**Why**: `rollback_linked_pages`'s own docstring (manager.rs:453-464) explains the
choice: distinguishing a CoW mark this call installed from one that pre-existed
(a re-fork of a frame still shared with an earlier child) cannot be done reliably
from PTE state or refcounts, so wrongly unmarking could break CoW for another
sharer. Leaving a page CoW that could have been writable only costs one extra CoW
fault, which is harmless. Hence the parent is **not** bit-for-bit restored on the
error path; some logically-writable parent pages may be left read-only with the
CoW bit set.

**Verification Failure**: Not a crash or overflow. The mismatch is between the
narrative contract ("`parent`/`child` restored to entry state") and the actual
best-effort, CoW-preserving rollback. A spec asserting
`final(parent)@ == old(parent)@ && final(child)@ == old(child)@` on `Err` would be
**unsound** (it claims behavior the code does not provide).

**How Verus Helped**: Forcing an explicit `Err` postcondition surfaced that the
"full rollback" wording is an overstatement: the only guarantee the code can
actually uphold on `Err` is that both address spaces remain well-formed
(`inv()`), not that they are byte-identical to entry.

**Severity**: cosmetic / correctness-preserving. The deliberate design choice is
safe (an abandoned fork's parent keeps working; stray CoW marks only cause a
redundant copy on the next write). No memory-safety or refcount-leak issue.

**Suggested Fix**: None to the code (the behavior is intentional and safe).
Instead the spec for `link_user_pages`'s `Err` arm captures only the provable
guarantee — `final(parent).inv() && final(child).inv()` — rather than full
restoration. The caller (`fork`) discards `child` and continues using `parent`,
which remains correct under this weaker guarantee. The caller-analysis/docstring
wording could be softened to "best-effort rollback; both spaces remain valid".

**Auto-Fixed**: No (intentional design; spec adjusted to match real behavior).

**What**: The draft `#[verus_spec]` on `ctrl_upage` omitted the

discharge `uctrl`'s requirement, so the function failed to verify.

**Why**: `ctrl_upage` only changes permissions on an existing mapping; it never
allocates. The "page already mapped" condition is a genuine caller obligation
(property FN-25 / LIVE-4), and the view design (view_design.md:302) lists it as a
precondition. The draft simply dropped it.

**How Verus Helped**: Removing `external_body` and translating the body produced a
precondition-not-satisfied error at the `uctrl` call site, pinpointing the missing
`requires`.

**Severity**: spec-only; no code defect. The code is correct given the (now
explicit) precondition.

**Auto-Fixed**: Yes — added
`vmem@.user_mapped(vaddr.addr_nat())` to `ctrl_upage`'s `requires`. The function
now verifies with a translated (non-`external_body`) body.

## Spec gap (fixed) — `new_vmem` missing `pgdir` distinctness (manager.rs:260, SB-2)

**What**: The draft `new_vmem` `Ok` arm omitted `new@.pgdir != vmem@.pgdir`
(property FN-2 / GLOBAL-4). Without it this module does not establish that a freshly
cloned address space gets its own page directory.

(FN-2/GLOBAL-4) and view design surfaced the omission.

those modules are verified; proving it then will require `Vmem::clone`'s contract
to be strengthened to expose `pgdir` freshness.

**Auto-Fixed**: Yes — added `new@.pgdir != vmem@.pgdir` to the `Ok` arm.
